blurb: Short-haired fawn Belgian Shepherd prized by police and military worldwide
description: The Malinois is the short-haired fawn variety of the Belgian Shepherd, a medium-sized, athletic herding dog from Belgium known for intelligence and drive.
answer: The Malinois is the short-haired, fawn variety of the Belgian Shepherd, a medium-sized herding dog from Belgium. Belgian Shepherds typically stand 56 to 66 cm and weigh 20 to 30 kg. The breed is described as highly intelligent, alert and trainable, and the Malinois is especially active.

body: The Belgian Shepherd descends from a common Western European shepherd type shared with the Dutch Shepherd and German Shepherd. By the late 1800s it was at risk of disappearing, and in 1891 the Club du Chien de Berger Belge was formed; a team led by Adolphe Reul surveyed the dogs and began standardizing them. The 1956 standard recognizes four varieties: Groenendael, Laekenois, Malinois and Tervueren. The Malinois, named for the Mechelen (Malines) region, was said to be the first variety to breed true to type. The FCI treats the four as one breed, while the AKC registers them as separate breeds.

The Belgian Shepherd is a medium-sized, athletic dog built for endurance, with a long head, triangular erect ears and a broad, long muzzle. The breed standard gives an ideal height of 62 cm for males and 58 cm for females. The Malinois has a short coat, fawn with black overlay, and a charcoal-colored face and extremities.

Belgian Shepherds are known as intelligent, alert and sensitive, typically highly trainable and hard-working, with a strong guarding instinct that makes them protective of property and family. The Malinois is described as particularly active, which may reflect its continued breeding for security roles.

All Belgian Shepherds need ample exercise and training, ideally from an early age, though the breed adapts well to living indoors. The Malinois is widely used by customs, military, border and police forces, including the US Secret Service and the anti-poaching unit at Kruger National Park.

The Société Royale Saint-Hubert recommends testing all varieties for hip and elbow dysplasia and testing the Malinois for epilepsy. Working lines of the Malinois have been associated with rage syndrome, for which genetic testing exists. A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12 years for the Malinois.

faq.q: Is a Malinois a separate breed from the Belgian Shepherd?
faq.a: Most kennel clubs, including the FCI, treat the Malinois as one of four varieties of the Belgian Shepherd, but the American Kennel Club recognizes it as a separate breed.

faq.q: How long do Belgian Malinois live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12 years for the Malinois.

faq.q: Why do police and the military use the Malinois?
faq.a: The breed is intelligent, highly trainable and vigilant, with a strong guarding instinct, which suits it to detection, patrol and security work.

faq.q: Is a Malinois a good family dog?
faq.a: Belgian Shepherds are protective of their families and adapt to indoor life, but the Malinois is very active and needs ample exercise and early training.
